statements.t: On February 28, 2025, we announced that we were actively engaged in discussions regarding the anticipated sale of our Products & Healthcare Services (P&HS) business.

While we believe that we will have the ability to meet our financing needs in the foreseeable future, changes in general economic conditions may impact: (i) the ability of financial institutions to meet their contractual commitments to us, (ii) the ability of our customers and suppliers to meet their obligations to us and (iii) our cost of borrowing.
Our liquidity forecasts are based upon successful execution of our value creation plan and includes management’s best estimate of the timing for achieving the benefits from the plan.
Assuming the continued execution of our value creation plan, we expect to remain in compliance with these covenants.

If we do not successfully achieve cost savings or experience an increase in revenues consistent with our projected timing under the value creation plan, additional capital sources may be required, the timing and source of which are uncertain.
We cannot provide any assurance as to if or when we will consummate any such transactions or the terms of any such transaction.
We do not intend to make use of the authorized repurchase program.

We have identified four key areas which are critical to our continued transformation and returning the business to the kind of profitability that our shareholders should expect” said Kenny Gardner-Smith, President & Chief Executive Officer, Accendra Health.
“We are already taking action on our turnaround, and, over the next several months, we will have our value creation plan fully underway.
The value creation plan is the cornerstone of returning the business to its potential, and we look forward to sharing details with all stakeholders in the coming months,” Gardner-Smith concluded.

The Company expects that full year net revenue will be at the bottom end of the prior outlook range of $2.45 billion to $2.55 billion and that adjusted EBITDA could be as much as 30% lower than the $310 million midpoint of the prior outlook range.

Although the Company provides guidance for adjusted EBITDA (which is a non-GAAP financial measure), it is not able to forecast the most directly comparable measures calculated and presented in accordance with GAAP without unreasonable effort.
Certain elements of the composition of the GAAP amounts are not predictable, making it impracticable for the Company to forecast.
As a result, no GAAP guidance or reconciliation of the Company’s adjusted EBITDA guidance is provided.
